_notes: Companion to db/protocols/rfc2305-duty-reservation.json -- see that file's _notes for provenance. Replaces ARCHITECTURE.md section 3's placeholder 'power: {budget: 400W}' with fields actually named in RFC-2305 section 6/section 14's PowerCapabilityRecord, for a Class-C constrained courier relay (section 2 scope: 'constrained devices with strict energy budgets... the usual Belter skiffs, wrist terminals'). What changed vs. the placeholder: the RFC deliberately does not mandate specific numbers ('does not mandate specific hardware power amplifiers' -- section 2) -- it mandates which fields a PowerCapabilityRecord must expose. So the power slot needed to become a structured record instead of a single budget number; a flat budget number genuinely couldn't express PowerClass, duty limits, or energy capacity as separate, independently-relevant facts. This is the kind of thing ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 predicted the real conversion would surface. Converted from YAML to JSON 2026-09-04 per project format decision.
_platform_id_note: PlatformID (a UUID-S7, per db/vocabulary.json) is deliberately absent here -- this file is a device type, not an instance. A specific node in node.json/network.json gets its own PlatformID when instantiated from this type.

power._notes: RFC-2305 section 6 PowerCapabilityRecord fields, section 14's required set

failure_modes._notes: gameplay shape, revised 2026-09-04 alongside the protocol file's HANDWAVE_TX/ADMISSION_PENDING split: a player (or an NPC originator) routing traffic down the cheap HANDWAVE_TX path when this node's policy actually required ADMISSION_PENDING's confirmed handshake -- traces to the RFC-2305 Companion's Trade-off A, framed as a discretion failure rather than a receipt-trust-window bug. Discoverable via probe/spec on this node's duty-reservation state and its power_policy_ref, not a scan flag.
